newsitem.title: GHANA: Banks, breweries sparkled on Ghana bourse in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Banks, breweries sparkled on Ghana bourse in 1996.

text.p: Banks and breweries were the star performers on the Ghana Stock Exchange in 1996, with some posting capital gains of up to 40 percent and 140 percent in the respective sectirs, an official bourse report showed.

The report gave no figure for the overall performance of the bourse, which fell by 13 percent in 1995 after two years of sharp climbs. Sentiment in the last quarter of 1996 was heavily dominated by concern over the domestic economy, notably inflation, and caution before national elections in December.
The star banks were Ghana Commercial Bank (GCB), whose market capitalisation of 115.67 billion cedis is second highest after Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd, and Social Security Bank (SSB).
New arrival GCB saw its 165 million shares rise in value by 40.2 percent while SSB's 71.25 million listed shares rose 31.5 percent, according to the official report released on Monday.
GCB's stock climbed from the 500 cedis offer price last May to close the year at 701 cedis. SSB, which began the year at 804 cedis in 1995, ended 1996 at 1,057 cedis.
The dividend yield for the two banks stood at 19.8 percent and 4.7 per cent respectively.
The growth in GCB was significant given that it went public only last May, the report noted.

The other bank on the exchange, Standard Chartered Bank Ltd, posted a dividend yield of eight percent, although its share price fell 13.8 percent. The stock fell from 5,800 cedis at the beginning of the year to 5,000 cedis on the last trading day.

Accra Brewery Ltd, one of the exchange's blue chips, made the highest capital gain in 1996. Its value rose 140 percent with its share price appreciating from 240 cedis at the beginning of the year to 576 cedis on December 30, 1996.

Guinness Ghana Ltd made a capital gain of 26.1 percent while the dividend yield rose by 2.7 per cent. The stock price of Guinness rose by 57 cedis, jumping from 218 cedis in 1995 to 275 cedis at the end of 1996.
Kumasi Brewery Ltd's capital gain was 9.1 percent while the dividend yield stood at 9.5 percent. Its share price ended at 660 cedis, up from the previous year's figure of 605 cedis.
Pioneer Aluminium Factory, Mobil Oil Ghana Ltd and Fan Milk Ltd, were the other risers on the market last year.

Pioneer recorded a capital gain of 25.7 percent on its 16.35 million issued shares while dividend yield per share was 3.5 percent. The company's share price finished 1996 at 171 cedis from 136 cedis quoted at the beginning of the year.

Mobil recorded a capital gain of 22.9 percent with a dividend yield of 15.7 percent. Fan Milk's capital gain was fixed at 22.4 per cent with a yield of 5.8 per cent on its share price which ended at 404 cedis compared with the previous year's close of 330 cedis.
Trading group CFAO was the biggest loser in terms of capital gain, going down 28.6 percent. The stock yielded no dividend.
